chunks: And from him, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Nawfali, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, he raised it (to the Imam) saying:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'When you see the new moon, do not depart (from this state/remembrance) and say: O God, I ask You for the goodness of this month, its light, its victory, its blessing, its purification, and its sustenance. And I ask You for the goodness that is in it and the goodness that is after it. And I seek refuge in You from the evil that is in it and the evil that is after it. O God, bring it to us with security, faith, safety, Islam, blessing, piety, and success for what You love and are pleased with.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْهِلَالُ: The new moon, marking the start of a lunar month

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication when seeing the new moon in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam Ali (AS) establishes a Sunnah for marking the lunar transition with specific dhikr, emphasizing the spiritual preparation for the month ahead. The supplication uniquely requests 'tahoor' (purification) and 'rizq' (sustenance), reflecting the Shia emphasis on both inner spiritual cleansing and divine provision as integral to the month's blessings.
